A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CapImagine research. Text and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The original appendices remain identifiable despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original latent-token interventions, probing experiments, CapImagine benchmark evaluations, ablations, and inference timings in Sections 3 and 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a matched-data Monet experiment, text-reasoning baseline comparisons, and evaluations on STARE and Hyperphantasia.

M1.justification: CapImagine retains the same caption-based rewriting, reasoning-chain refinement, filtering to 17K examples, and supervised fine-tuning procedure. The backbone and proposed inference approach are unchanged; the new Monet experiment is an evaluation control.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds STARE transformations, cube nets, tangrams, temporal reasoning, and perspective tasks, plus Hyperphantasia interpolation and trajectory-extrapolation puzzles. These substantially broaden abstract visual reasoning requirements beyond the retained perception, BLINK, TableVQA, and latent-analysis tasks.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds PAPO, Vision-R1, R1-OneVision, and LLaVA-OneVision comparisons on retained benchmarks, introducing a substantial text-reasoning comparator category. Tables 6–7 also include previously absent comparators such as Claude-3.5 Sonnet, Gemini-2.0 Flash, and o4-mini. Existing comparator rows remain.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds a controlled experiment using the complete Monet training pipeline on CapImagine's same curated 17K subset. New evaluations specify STARE without visual simulation and Hyperphantasia accuracy by difficulty. CapImagine's previously stated training configuration remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The new data-parity ablation tests whether CapImagine's advantage persists when Monet uses the same selected training examples. It supplements the existing rewriting and filtering ablations; the latent interventions, probing, dependency analysis, and efficiency analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 7's new means aggregate puzzle accuracies, while the added noise-distribution detail specifies an intervention rather than uncertainty around results.

E6.justification: Previously reported scores are retained, while the Monet subset row and Tables 5–7 add substantial results. The subset Monet scores 79.6 on V* versus CapImagine's 85.9. New STARE overall scores are 40.7 versus Monet's 35.3. Hyperphantasia means favor CapImagine on easy and medium tasks but favor Monet on hard tasks, 20.25 versus 22.25.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3, the inference definitions, and the causal formulation remain unchanged. Correcting Section 3.2's heading from X→Y to X→Z aligns its label with the existing analysis; it does not revise mathematical reasoning. No proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: two latent-reasoning disconnects, limited latent semantics, and CapImagine's effectiveness as a text-space alternative. Added experiments provide evidence for the existing effectiveness and generality claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D explicitly limits 'NOT YET' to current representative LVR implementations and argues that fixing degeneration requires new training paradigms. Section 5.3 adds an interpretation of the data-parity control. Appendix C extends the generalization argument, although its 'consistent advantage' wording overlooks losses in Tables 6–7. Existing limitations move from Appendix C to E.

D1.justification: v2 adds an open-source statement and project repository link. Section 3.3.1 newly specifies matching intervention noise to latent tokens' empirical mean and standard deviation. This adds implementation documentation; unchanged results and retained zero-mean notation do not establish whether the existing intervention implementation changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting PAPO, Vision-R1, STARE, Hyperphantasia, CRYSTAL, and PonderLM-2, alongside other citation changes, and removes Being-H0.5 and DeepPerception. Appendix D clarifies the diagnostic positioning toward current LVR implementations. The related-work taxonomy and most discussion remain intact.

P1.justification: Changes include the corrected Section 3.2 heading, a Summary subheading, labeled ablation paragraphs, new appendix sections, and affiliation, publication-footer, and acknowledgement edits. Most existing prose and the main argument's sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a Monet-subset row, and Appendix C adds Tables 5–7. Figures 1–6 retain their graphical content, while captions for Figures 2 and 5 are expanded. Existing tables and figures relocate through page reflow without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the comparison with a matched-17K Monet control that v1 lacked, text-reasoning baselines, and additional mental-visualization tests. These reduce a data-selection confound and broaden empirical support. The benefit is tempered by sparse settings for the added comparisons and an overbroad 'consistent advantage' interpretation: Table 7 reports a lower hard-level mean for CapImagine than Monet, 20.25 versus 22.25. The added evidence and clearer scope support a limited net quality gain.
